note: CVS's own 2027 formulary documents (dated 2026-10-01) drop Vascepa for generic IPE. Nobody has linked them to Amarin, and the Q3 call is the first place 2027 exclusivity can come up. Trading below net cash partly offsets this.
The guide arithmetic points to a modest beat and a possible raise. Against that, the stock ran 21% in 5 days with no news, and 2026 beat-and-reiterate prints were sold. Close to balanced.

Street revenue consensus ($154-156M, two sources) sits below the floor of the company's own Q3 guide ($158-168M), and the company landed at the top of its guide last quarter. The unresolved Arcadia put caps this.
The Albertsons sale gain should lift headline GAAP EPS and book value at 45% of undepreciated book, with a 13D holder now pushing. Dividend-coverage commentary and office impairments offset it.

Brent and bunker prices spiked after the July cut to the cost-pressure estimate, which puts the $230-240M EBITDA guide at risk. That is a proxy and partly priced by the 13% slide. A habitual EPS beat partly offsets it.

The company's own safe-harbor disclosures ($202M of agreements against about $194M recognised or guided) imply a roughly $75M Q4 cliff, and a flat Q4 consensus does not show it. A 22% short interest and the put skew damp this.
The 25% run-up comes from one passive 13D buyer, so a release with no deal may give some of it back. The strategic-review status is a two-sided stub.
A beat of the guide is likely but sits inside what the company guided. The 30% sector-driven run-up has raised the bar. Skew is balanced.

Q3 same-store sales were pre-signalled above 3% and should land in guide. Sell-side cuts lowered the bar, and short interest is about 22-26% of the real float. The QSR peer weakness is already in the put skew.

The H1 run-rate (+14-15%) against FY consensus at the guide midpoint sets up a third beat-and-raise, and this name's beat-and-raise prints have been bought. Unlike last year's miss, there was no pre-announcement. Squadron's overhang offsets a little.
There is no bar. The tax-line reversion, the funding squeeze and new-CFO risk offset the improving credit indicators and the unexplained 42% HK premium, so the net is balanced.
The FY guide needs a record Q4, so a trim is a live risk on a name that moves violently on its guide. An easy Q3 comp and no covenant pressure partly offset it.

TTF gas roughly doubled (to about EUR90) after O-I last guided, with part of Q4 and about half of 2027 unhedged, on a name that fell 15% on each of the last two energy-driven guide cuts. Ardagh's North America shipments were -6%. Despite this the stock ran +13% into the print.
The shrinking originations base sits below the H2 run-rate the guide needs, which risks a second trim. About 17% of float is short at the 52-week low, and Enova's healthy credit print partly offsets.
The H1 constant-currency pace against a soft Q3 comp makes a revenue beat or raise plausible. It is nearly offset by the H2 EBITDA step-up the unchanged guide requires.

The FY guide needs a $240-255M Q4 while the Verizon voice program has slipped again. This is also the first covenant test after a waiver. The 30% drawdown and the IP Optical bookings partly offset it.
Launch commentary covers only four weeks, the quarter shows no revenue, and the stock ran 13% with calls bid. A 26% short interest offsets this, so the net is close to balanced.

Under the company's own DE definition, the first realized loss (the Dallas discount, about $0.067 a share) points to DE of $0.17-0.18 against the $0.23-0.25 guide. A Q4 coverage path and a price already discounting a cut partly offset it.
A cat-free Q3 means a large EPS beat and room to raise the guide, but last year's identical beat was sold. The +28% run-up above analyst targets and the Isaias Q4 retention risk offset most of it.

Lam's +22% sequential quarter points to a top-end Q3 beat, but Lam's December deceleration points to a soft first Q4 guide on a name that has sold all five recorded prints. The 37% drawdown has partly priced that in.
